body: This is [normal TypeScript semantics](http://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/classes.html#parameter-properties), Angular was not involved at all.

Hi Trotyl/Jose,

Thanks for your clarifications.

I am still learning TypeScript. Now, I realize that I need to catch up with
TypeScript even deeper.

Regards,
  --Sreenivasulu Saya


On Fri, Apr 20, 2018 at 2:39 PM, José Toledo Navarro <
notifications@github.com> wrote:

> Someone coming from the OOP background, they think that it is just a
> formal parameter and expects it to be initialized with the instance of the
> object created with new operator.
>
> Im pretty sure that most devs will recognize that the component is using
> constructor injection.
>
> Looks like, in Angular, by virtue of specifying it as a formal parameter
> to constructor method it automatically does the following:
> private service: HeroService;
> constructor() {
> service = new HeroService();
> }
>
> Not sure where did you got this idea from, but its incorrect. @trotyl
> <https://github.com/trotyl> already pointed out how parameter properties
> work.
>

Hi Jennifer,

Thanks for accepting my feedback. Including in the introductory material
would be a good idea.

Definitely, documenting the missing pieces in the documentation will hep to
understand Angular better and hence it will be embraced with more comfort
by the development community.

Regards,
